protocol: §6.N.2 production-code-coverage hunt — pick 2 fresh gate-shaping files (filter: would a bug here be invisible to existing tests?), apply ONE non-crashing mutation per file that changes user-visible/observable behavior, run the module test, confirm RED on user-visible state (or surviving GREEN = GAP), revert.

files_hunted.production_path: SyncPeriod.flexIntervalMillis — the flex-interval mapping WorkBackgroundService.periodicWorkRequest() feeds into WorkManager's PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder(repeat, flex). The flex window is the tail-of-period during which the periodic sync (favorites / bookmarks / history / credentials) runs. WorkManager requires flexInterval <= repeatInterval; a flex larger than the repeat is silently clamped to the full period, degrading the user's sync schedule from 'run near the end of the period' to 'run anytime in the period'.
files_hunted.mutation: SyncPeriod.flexIntervalMillis: SyncPeriod.DAY -> 6.hours  =>  SyncPeriod.DAY -> 6.days (the historical 6.days-for-6.hours regression the test's KDoc names; flex 6 days > repeat 1 day → WorkManager clamps, destroying the DAY flex window).
observed_failure_verbatim: SyncPeriodIntervalsTest > DAY sync flex is six hours, not six days FAILED
SyncPeriodIntervalsTest > flex interval never exceeds repeat interval for any periodic SyncPeriod FAILED

java.lang.AssertionError: SyncPeriod.DAY: flexInterval (518400000 ms) MUST be <= repeatInterval (86400000 ms) or WorkManager clamps it to the full period, destroying the flex window  (SyncPeriodIntervalsTest.kt:46)
files_hunted.red_then_green: 2 of 3 tests RED with mutation; reverted (6.days -> 6.hours); :core:work:impl:testDebugUnitTest BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
files_hunted.verdict_reason: SyncPeriodIntervalsTest provably catches the user-visible-schedule-degradation break it claims to cover. Primary assertions are on the actual ms values WorkManager consumes (518400000 vs 21600000 / 86400000). The documented falsifiability rehearsal in the test's KDoc is verified real, not a bluff-claim.

files_hunted.production_path: ConnectionsViewModel.observeConnections() — the onCreate collector that consumes observeEndpointsStatusUseCase() and reduces it into ConnectionsState.selected (the active-endpoint highlight a user sees) + ConnectionsState.connections (the rendered connection list). This is the user-visible 'which API/endpoint is active + here are all your endpoints' surface.

files_hunted.mutation: observeConnections() reduce: `selected = connections.firstOrNull(EndpointState::selected)` => `selected = connections.firstOrNull { !it.selected }` (highlight points at the WRONG, non-selected endpoint) AND `connections = connections` => `connections = emptyList()` (the rendered connection list is always empty).

files_hunted.verdict_reason: A real user-visible defect — wrong active-endpoint highlight + empty connection list — was invisible to the existing suite. Per §6.N this is a coverage GAP, closed by a new falsifiable real-stack test.

state.selected == the selected=true row (the active-endpoint highlight), NOT the first-in-list unselected row
